Subject: Evening micro-webinar: staggered entry + standby list process

Hi Sarah & Tom —

Thanks again for the interest. We have a 45-minute micro-webinar planned for the evening of June 24 to walk through short, focused example flows (prefix caching, quantization tradeoffs, and a quick live Q&A). Because we expect a few overlapping prospect signups, I want to propose a staggered entry + standby process so no single attendee blocks the live demo.

Proposed flow:
- 6:00–6:05pm PT: quick intro and expectations
- 6:05–6:25pm PT: demo split into two 10-minute segments; we admit prospects in waves
- 6:25–6:45pm PT: live Q&A — open to everyone on the bridge

Standby rules (short):
1) If more than 12 registered, we admit first 12 on audio/video for the demo; others join in observer-only mode and rotated into the Q&A.
2) If someone drops before 6:05, we pull the next person from the standby list at the 30s mark.
3) We will record the session and share the short clip and a 1-pager.

Attachments: micro-webinar-agenda.pdf (local), standby-process.md (ops notes) — shared for internal ops and prospect view.

Quick asks:
- Sarah: confirm if you need a 5:30pm PT slot instead (I can shuffle hosts).
- Soojin: can you host the bridge and manage admission logic?
- Marissa: can you take notes/Q&A triage?

Thanks — aiming to keep this tight and low-friction.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
